explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/126 with the positive answer (formal proof linked): f(n)/log n → ∞, where f(n) is the largest m such that every n-element A ⊆ ℕ has ∏_{a≠b}(a+b) with at least m distinct prime factors. Ordered offDiag pairs only square the product, leaving its prime factors unchanged. Allowing 0 ∈ A changes f by at most one index, since f_0(n) ≥ f_{>0}(n-1) (0 + b = b), so the asymptotics are unaffected.
